## Testing Standards

- TDD is MANDATORY — a failing test is written before implementation. pytest via
`uv run pytest`; tests live in tests/. Extractors and schema logic are covered
with table-driven tests and fixtures.

- **Hard-case regression rule:** whenever a document (or document *type*) fails or
misbehaves in the pipeline, ADD IT to `config/hard-cases.yaml` so we never regress
on it. Run the isolated suite with `uv run goldberg test-hard-cases` (extraction,
no live index, no OpenAI cost) — it gates the bulk re-ingest. Synthesize adversarial
documents (`goldberg_system.testing.synthetic`) to probe limits before a real
document exposes them. See `doc/runbooks/hard-case-testing.md`.

- **End-to-end tests for major components (mandatory):** every major component — the
extraction path, the enrichment/index pipeline, the query layer, the observability
surface, the MCP server — must have an end-to-end test in addition to its unit tests.
The E2E test **exercises the component against its real integrations** (Docling,
Elasticsearch, the manifest — an isolated `*_test` index, never the live corpus) to
prove the pieces fit together, and it **guards performance**: it records timing and
fails (or flags) on a major regression, so a change that silently makes ingestion or
query dramatically slower is caught. Unit tests prove the logic; E2E tests prove the
integration and the speed.


## Quality Gates

- Blocking before a work package is approved/merged: all tests green, ruff clean,
black-formatted, mypy clean.


## Performance Benchmarks

- A batch document pipeline: throughput and correctness matter more than latency.
Ingestion is idempotent and scoped per-document (not corpus-wide) on each
trigger. CLI operations stay responsive.


## Branch Strategy

- Mission work goes through the Spec Kitty spec -> plan -> tasks -> implement ->
review -> merge flow; every work package is reviewed before merge.

- Deployment constraints: Runs on the Halob NAS (192.168.86.31); services shipped as docker-compose. All
four repos are private and hold legally-sensitive material. The corpus lives on
the NAS specifically so file changes can trigger the pipeline via a Halob-local
filesystem watcher (not a GitHub webhook).

## Policy Summary

- Intent: A defence research + drafting tool for a live UK private prosecution —
R (Goldberg) v Mannino, Edwards and Fadhley — in which the user is one of the
defendants. An automated, idempotent pipeline turns raw legal documents into a
searchable, LLM-queryable, ATTRIBUTED knowledge base, to (1) answer attributed
questions across the evidence corpus (grounded, with citations to source
document + raw commit + speaker + date) and (2) draft responses to the court
and other parties grounded in that corpus and the user's own prior research.
Attributed Q&A and cross-corpus contradiction detection (surfacing where a
party's account shifts over time) are BOTH first-class. Runs on the Halob NAS.
This repo is the pipeline + tooling; it is one of four repos (raw / extracted /
casework / system) with distinct lifecycles.

- Languages/Frameworks: Python 3.12+, uv for dependency management and execution. Core libs: click
(CLI), pydantic (models/validation), pyyaml + python-frontmatter (metadata).
Runtime services on Halob: Elasticsearch (index goldberg_files) and NATS,
shipped via docker-compose. LLM/RAG: cloud OpenAI/Anthropic for enrichment and
Ragie for the RAG sink. Reuse Mind of Steele (llm_support, elasticsearch,
ragie_uploader) as a git source / vendored package rather than reinventing.

- Testing: TDD is MANDATORY — a failing test is written before implementation. pytest via
`uv run pytest`; tests live in tests/. Extractors and schema logic are covered
with table-driven tests and fixtures.

- Quality Gates: Blocking before a work package is approved/merged: all tests green, ruff clean,
black-formatted, mypy clean.

- Review Policy: Mission work goes through the Spec Kitty spec -> plan -> tasks -> implement ->
review -> merge flow; every work package is reviewed before merge.

- Performance Targets: A batch document pipeline: throughput and correctness matter more than latency.
Ingestion is idempotent and scoped per-document (not corpus-wide) on each
trigger. CLI operations stay responsive.

- Deployment Constraints: Runs on the Halob NAS (192.168.86.31); services shipped as docker-compose. All
four repos are private and hold legally-sensitive material. The corpus lives on
the NAS specifically so file changes can trigger the pipeline via a Halob-local
filesystem watcher (not a GitHub webhook).


## Project Directives

1. Respect risk boundaries: Highest-cost failures first: (1) PROVENANCE LOSS — every derived doc and ES
record must link back to its exact raw path + commit sha (non-negotiable, legal
case); (2) MUTATION OF goldberg-raw — raw is immutable/sacred, extraction
failures dead-letter and never touch it; (3) LEAKAGE beyond the private repos —
be deliberate about what goes to GitHub vs Halob-only; (4) NON-IDEMPOTENCY /
duplication — deterministic doc-ids so re-ingest updates, never duplicates.
Legal-handling flags (cpia_s17, privileged, sensitivity, disclosure_status,
source_channel) are HUMAN-authored and default to the safe value when absent;
the LLM must not invent them.

2. Keep documentation synchronized with workflow and behavior changes:
**Every material change to the system MUST include a corresponding documentation
change** — no code, behaviour, schema, pipeline-topology, or deployment change
lands without updating the relevant doc(s) (design.md / workflow.md /
architecture.md / the affected runbook / an ADR for decisions) in the same unit
of work. A change is "material" if it alters how the system behaves, is
operated, is queried, or is reasoned about; pure internal refactors with no
behavioural or interface change are exempt. doc/ is the human-facing design
record, maintained directly (see doc/design.md for the corpus model, metadata
schema, and ingest paths). Keep canonical terms precise: `matters`
(multi-valued case identifiers), `origin`/`role` (the two-axis taxonomy),
`author`/`source_party` (who is speaking, vs `parties` = who a doc is about).

## Amendment Process

The charter is amended via /spec-kitty.charter; substantive design decisions are
recorded in doc/ (design.md) as the human-facing record.


## Exception Policy

Deviations are recorded explicitly, never taken silently. Standing exception:
legally-sensitive material (CPIA s.17, personal data, unofficially-obtained
material) MAY be sent to cloud OpenAI/Anthropic + Ragie for enrichment and RAG —
a deliberate, logged data-boundary exception accepted for capability.
